name: Ahijah
bio: Ahijah the Shilonite was a prophet who met Solomon's official Jeroboam alone in a field outside Jerusalem. Wearing a new cloak, Ahijah tore it into twelve pieces and told Jeroboam to take ten of them, declaring that the LORD was about to tear ten tribes of the kingdom away from Solomon and give them to Jeroboam, as judgment for Solomon's idolatry — though one tribe would remain with Solomon's son for David's sake. Ahijah promised that if Jeroboam obeyed the LORD as David had, the LORD would build him an enduring dynasty and give him Israel (1 Kings 11:29-39). Ahijah's prophecy set in motion the division of Solomon's kingdom. Years later, now blind with age, he was visited by Jeroboam's wife, disguised to protect her identity, who came to ask about her sick son Abijah. The LORD told Ahijah in advance who was coming, and he recognized her by the sound of her footsteps before she even spoke. Ahijah delivered a harsh second prophecy: because Jeroboam had made idols and provoked the LORD to anger, far exceeding the wickedness of anyone before him, the LORD would utterly destroy his entire house, and Israel itself would one day be uprooted and scattered beyond the Euphrates for the sins Jeroboam had led the nation into. Ahijah told her that the boy would die the moment she returned home — which happened exactly as he said (1 Kings 14:1-18). His prophecy of Jeroboam's house being utterly wiped out was fulfilled a few years later, when Baasha assassinated Jeroboam's son and successor Nadab and exterminated every remaining member of the family (1 Kings 15:27-29).
